findings.detail: Two source-sanctioned substitutions, both taken from alternatives the page itself offers: Gouda -> shredded cheddar ('or use cheddar') and sugar-free BBQ sauce -> regular BBQ sauce ('or your favorite'). Pulled pork (source assumed pre-made, 12 oz cooked) is booked as 4 1/2 lb raw pork shoulder cooked and pulled; 2041 g raw at ~58% yield lands at the scaled 1191 g cooked target. All documented in writer_notes. No invented or dropped ingredients.

One ratio 4->14 (3.5x) holds: peppers 1 lb->1588 g exact, cheese 6 oz->21 oz/595 g exact, cilantro 2 tbsp->7 tbsp exact, pork 12 oz cooked->1191 g cooked equivalent via raw shoulder. BBQ sauce 1/3 cup x3.5 = 1.17 cups, booked as 1 1/4 cups (356 g), implied ratio 3.75 - ordinary rounding to a shoppable quarter-cup, not a hand-adjusted line.

Method survives: soften peppers, mix sauce + most cheese into pork, fill, bake ~20 min, top with reserved cheese, melt, cilantro garnish. Added steps (cook/shred the raw shoulder; explicit halve-and-seed, which the source implies via 'the cut peppers' but never states; weigh-and-divide portioning) extend rather than change the dish. Time rebuilt to ~4h20m for the raw-shoulder build, honestly flagged.
